group_min.note: Parks Canada lists seasonal access restrictions in Banff only for Bryant Creek/Allenby Pass, the Lake Minnewanka area trails and the Moraine Lake area trails; Lake Agnes is not among them (read 25 Oct 2026). Restrictions can be added at short notice.

age_band.note: 7.8 km and 495 m (effort_km 12.75) against the age gates of suitability.md 6.2: over the 6-7 ceiling (6 km, 350 m), inside the 8-9 ceiling (9 km, 500 m, 14).

suitability.kid_note: A steady climb from the Lake Louise shore past Mirror Lake to a seasonal tea house on Lake Agnes. The last stretch is a flight of steps beside a waterfall. Little Beehive and Big Beehive are side trips.

carrier_ok.note: 495 m of climb is over the carrying-adult ceiling of suitability.md 6.2 (8 km, 400 m).

stroller.note: A Moderate mountain trail with 495 m of climb; the page does not mention strollers.

wheelchair.note: A Moderate mountain trail with 495 m of climb; the page gives no accessibility detail.

distance_km.note: 3.9 km one way, so 7.8 km return.

loss_m.note: Loss on the way up, as Parks Canada states it.

exposure.note: A forest trail and steps to a lake basin; the Beehive side trips are not part of this record.

v.note: Avalanche terrain: Parks Canada says the teahouse hikes are not safe from November through mid-May
Parks Canada shuttle to the Lake Louise Lakeshore from the Park and Ride; a reservation is required (2026 dates).
Paid parking at the lakeshore in shuttle season; the lot often fills before sunrise. Parks Canada says not to hike to Lake Agnes in winter or spring (avalanche terrain, November to mid-May).

food.quote: open mid-May and close after Canadian Thanksgiving in mid-October
food.note: A privately run tea house at the lake.

navigation.note: A maintained Parks Canada trail with junctions to the Beehives; signage is not described on the page.

dogs.quote: Dogs are allowed on all trails in the summer unless otherwise specified in trail restrictions and closures.
dogs.note: No restriction was listed for the Lake Agnes Trail when read. The national-park rule is a leash at all times.

group_min.note: Alberta Parks gives a group size limit of 15 for this trail (a maximum); it states no minimum.

age_band.note: 7.8 km and 320 m (effort_km 11.0) against the age gates of suitability.md 6.2: over the 6-7 ceiling (6 km), inside the 8-9 ceiling (9 km, 500 m, 14).

suitability.kid_note: A long, steady climb through subalpine forest from the Upper Kananaskis Lake shore to a lake under the Sarrail headwall.

carrier_ok.note: 7.8 km and 320 m is inside the carrying-adult ceiling of suitability.md 6.2 (8 km, 400 m, effort 12).

stroller.note: A climbing forest trail; the OSM ways are tagged unpaved, with a short wooden section. The official page does not mention strollers.

distance_km.note: 3.9 km one way, so 7.8 km return. Alberta Parks counts from the Upper Lake Trail, which the route follows first.

conflicts.note: Computed from the OSM ways named Rawson Lake Trail (24836168, 181184079, 181184081), 2.47 km from the Rawson Lake Trailhead node 269822212 to the lake shore, doubled; Overpass run api-2026-10-25-data-d3a-overpass. It leaves out the Upper Lake Trail approach that the official figure includes.

gain_m.note: Alberta Parks gives both units; the metre figure is used.

surface.note: OSM tags surface=unpaved on the trail ways and surface=wood on a 168 m section; unpaved is recorded as dirt. The official page is silent.

adult_time_min.note: Estimate, not stated by Alberta Parks: Naismith's rule on the official 7.8 km and 320 m (5 km/h plus 1 h per 600 m of climb) gives 125 min, widened to 180 min for a stop at the lake.

exposure.note: Alberta Parks describes a forest climb to a lake.

navigation.note: Leaves the Upper Lake Trail at a junction; signage is not described on the page.

dogs.quote: All pets are required to be leashed no more than 2 metres, or caged, at all times
dogs.note: The Alberta provincial-park rule; the trail report does not mention dogs.

group_min.note: Sulphur Mountain is not on Parks Canada's list of Banff areas with seasonal access restrictions (read 25 Oct 2026).

age_band.note: About 1 km and 368 shallow steps in each direction: any age, the youngest carried.

suitability.kid_note: A ridge boardwalk from the gondola's upper terminal toward Sanson's Peak, with 368 shallow steps in each direction. It now ends at a viewpoint between the Cosmic Ray Station and the old weather observatory.

carrier_ok.note: About 1 km return is far inside the carrying-adult ceiling.

stroller.note: The operator says this of the cabins and mountaintop facilities; the boardwalk has 368 steps in each direction.

wheelchair.quote: the summit boardwalk is not as it consists of 368 shallow stairs
wheelchair.note: The gondola and the summit building are wheelchair accessible; the boardwalk is not.

distance_km.note: Parks Canada gives 0.5 km from the top of the gondola to Sanson Peak, so 1.0 km return.

conflicts.note: The operator calls it 'a casual 2 km stroll to Sanson's Peak'; whether that is return is not said. The FAQ says the boardwalk now ends short of the observatory.

tried: https://www.banffjaspercollection.com/attractions/banff-gondola/faqs/ (368 shallow stairs in each direction; no metres)
gain_m.note: The steps go up and down along the ridge; no published climb in metres.

exposure.note: A boardwalk on an open ridge; neither page says whether it is railed or how steep the drops are.

v.note: Hazardous avalanche terrain lies beside the Sulphur Mountain trail in winter; ice cleats are recommended when icy
The Banff Gondola runs year-round except for a short maintenance period each November.

access_season.quote: open year-round, except for a short maintenance period each November

navigation.note: A single boardwalk from the upper terminal; nothing to choose.

dogs.quote: Pets are not permitted on the gondola or in our facilities, with the exception of service dogs
dogs.note: This covers the gondola and the summit building. Whether a dog walked up the Sulphur Mountain trail may use the boardwalk is not stated.

suitability.carrier_ok.note: 2.2 km and 85 m is far inside the carrying-adult ceiling.

set.suitability.kid_note: A paved trail and catwalks bolted to the canyon wall to the Lower Falls; busy, with narrow sections. The Upper Falls are 1.3 km further and 130 m higher.

v.where: the catwalks along the canyon wall

suitability.exposure.note: The plan's own note calls the catwalks exposed; Parks Canada's table does not say whether they are railed, so fenced stays null.

ext.navigation.note: One paved canyon trail from the P1 lot to the Lower Falls; nothing to choose.

suitability.effort.drivers.distance_km.c.note: The winter walking page gives 1.2 km one way to the Lower Falls (the summer table 1.1 km).

suitability.effort.drivers.gain_m.confli.note: The winter walking page gives 50 m to the Lower Falls (the summer table 85 m gain, 55 m loss).

suitability.wheelchair.note: Parks Canada gives 100% paved and a typical width of 182 cm to the Lower Falls, 8 accessible stalls and flush toilets at the trailhead, but calls the trail busy with narrow sections and gives no maximum grade for this stretch (30% on the way to the Upper Falls). Not stated as accessible, so partial.

v.note: Parks Canada lists Johnston Canyon among its winter walks: usually very icy, ice cleats strongly recommended.
The Bow Valley Parkway is closed 8 p.m. to 8 a.m. on the 17 km east of Johnston Canyon Campground; reach the lot from the west at night.

suitability.access_season.note: 2026 only: the trail, day-use area and P1 lot are closed 13 Oct to 11 Dec 2026 for rock-slope work (bulletin pc-closure-jc); the Upper Falls and Ink Pots stay reachable by the Moose Meadows trail. A one-off, not a yearly closure.
